blockSender.reason: Blocking a sender makes or changes a contact, which lives with the other contacts rather than under /contacts/block.

createAccount.reason: The account is read and changed through the admin mailbox routes; DELETE /accounts/{id} gives up a link to an account and does not delete it.

linkAccount.reason: What linking makes is the caller's access to an account, read and given up at the account's own path rather than under /accounts/link.

saveDraft.reason: A draft is a message: it is read and deleted through the message routes, and only its change and its send are draft routes.

sendMessage.reason: A send answers the message it saved, which lives under the message routes rather than under /messages/send.

activateGrant.*: Starts a timed use of a grant that already exists: there is no activation to read or change by id, and ending it takes a second factor in the body of deactivateGrant.

addInstallationSenderRule.read: No route reads one installation sender rule: listInstallationSenderRules reads the installation's entries.
addInstallationSenderRule.update: An installation sender rule is changed by removing it and adding its replacement; there is no update route.

addToAllowlist.read: No route reads one entry: listAllowlist is the read of a domain's entries.
addToAllowlist.update: An entry is only a pattern; changing one is removing it and adding another.

addToBlocklist.read: No route reads one entry: listBlocklist is the read of a domain's entries.
addToBlocklist.update: An entry is only a pattern; changing one is removing it and adding another.

blockSender.read: No route reads one contact: listContacts is the read of a mailbox's contacts.

createAPIKey.read: No route reads one key, and its secret is shown once: listAPIKeys is the read of an account's keys.

createAppPassword.read: No route reads one app password, and its secret is shown once: listCredentials is the read.
createAppPassword.update: An app password has nothing to change: it is revoked and another is made.

createBan.read: No route reads one ban: listBans is the read of the bans in force.
createBan.update: A ban is changed by creating it again, which answers 200 with the ban replaced.

createCertificate.update: No route changes a certificate: a replacement is a new upload, and the old one is deleted.

createClientSecret.read: No route reads one client secret, and its secret is shown once: listClientSecrets is the read.
createClientSecret.update: A client secret has nothing to change: it is revoked and another is made.

createContact.read: No route reads one contact: listContacts is the read of a mailbox's contacts.

createFolder.read: No route reads one folder: listFolders reads a mailbox's folders and listMessages a folder's contents.

createGrant.read: No route reads one grant: listGrants is the read of the grants a caller may see.
createGrant.update: A grant's mode changes only through activateGrant, deactivateGrant and makeGrantEligible, each taking a fresh second factor in its body, so no answer can fill them.

createImportSession.read: No route reads an open session: its counts are written once, as the summary closeImportSession answers and audits.
createImportSession.update: A session has nothing a client changes: each importMessage with its id counts into it, and closing it ends it.

createPipeline.read: No route reads one pipeline: listPipelines is the read of the pipelines an administrator may see.

deliverMessage.*: Machine to machine delivery: the caller is a gateway with no access to the mailbox it delivered into, so the message routes are not its to follow.

forwardMessage.*: A send that is often scheduled (202 answers a schedule, not a message); sendMessage links the lifecycle of the message a send saves.

inviteAccount.*: An invitation is a one-time token shown once: it has no id to read, change or delete, and issuing another invalidates it.

linkAccount.update: A link has no fields of its own to change: it exists or it does not.

putSieveScript.update: This PUT is itself the update: it creates the script or replaces it at the same path.

receiveTlsReport.*: A public ingest for other servers' TLS reports: its answer says only that the report was stored, with no id, and administrators read reports through /api/v1/admin/tls-reports.

registerPushDevice.read: No route reads one device: listPushDevices is the read of the caller's devices.
registerPushDevice.update: Registering the same token again is the update: it answers 200 with the device refreshed.

registerRecoveryEmail.delete: No route removes a recovery address: registering another is the only change an account can make to it.
registerRecoveryEmail.update: Registering again is the update: it replaces the address and clears its verification.

restmailDeliver.*: Server to server delivery: the sending server has no access to the mailbox it delivered into, so nothing here is its to follow.

saveDraft.delete: deleteMessage deletes a draft, but is not linked from here. saveDraft comes before sendMessage in the description and a sequenced contract run follows the first link, so this link would point deleteMessage's example at a draft, which sendDraft consumes in the message ownership run. TestCreatesPersistAndEndAt404 still proves a draft's delete.
saveDraft.read: getMessage reads a draft, but is not linked from here. Its answer links getThread, which claims a thread, and a new draft that replies to nothing has an empty thread_id. sendMessage links getMessage, and a sent message always has a thread. TestCreatesPersistAndEndAt404 still proves a draft's read.
saveDraft.update: updateDraft is a draft's change and is linked; updateMessage changes a saved message's flags and folder, not a draft's contents.

sendDraft.*: A send that deletes the draft it sends and is often scheduled (202 answers a schedule, not a message); sendMessage links the lifecycle of the message a send saves.

sendTestEmail.*: A test-environment route that injects a message for a contract or end-to-end test to look for: its answer is a report and not a resource.

setMtaStsPolicy.update: This PUT is itself the update: it creates the policy or replaces it at the same path.

unsubscribeMailto.*: A send of the message a mailto: unsubscribe target asks for, often held by a send limit (202 answers a hold, not a message); sendMessage links the lifecycle of the message a send saves.
